**Extract:**

**Titantic Toys (TT)**

TT is a large manufacturer of toys based in country Y. It is a public limited company and has been trading for 20 years. TT’s products are designed for children up to the age of 5.

TT has benefited from economies of scale as it has grown. The company has been able to buy specialist new equipment for the flow production line in its factory. TT’s factory uses lean production methods, such as Kaizen and just-in-time inventory control. All of its employees are well-motivated and few leave each year. The company provides training for employees in all departments of the business whenever there are any changes such as introducing new equipment or new products.

Currently, TT only sells its products in country Y but it plans to expand into country Z and become a multinational company. TT could buy a toy manufacturer located in country Z or build its own factory there. The government of country Z will need to give permission for TT to build a new factory. Either option will cost \$10 million. The directors are worried about liquidity as TT expands.

TT has developed a new toy for children under 5. The toy is a soft, easy to hold doll which speaks 4 different languages. The Marketing Director thinks this new toy will help TT expand into country Z, as there are no other products like it in that country. TT is recruiting a new Marketing Manager for country Z. Details of the shortlisted applicants are in Appendix 3.

The marketing department has already carried out research in country Z and some results are shown in Appendix 1.

**Appendix 1 **

**Market research results for country Z**

**Appendix 2 **

**Extract from TT’s statement of financial position, 2021 and 2022 (at 31 March)**

|   | **2021 (\$m)** | **2022 (\$m)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Inventories** | 5 | 5 |
| **Accounts receivable (debtors)** | 5 | 8 |
| **Cash** | 0 | 2 |
|   | {align=center} | {align=center} |
| **Accounts payable (creditors)** | 4 | 5 |
| **Bank overdraft** | 1 | 0 |
|   | {align=center} | {align=center} |
| **Long-term bank loans** | 5 | 10 |
|   | {align=center} | {align=center} |
| **Total Shareholder’s equity** | 40 | 50 |
|   | {align=center} | {align=center} |
| **Current ratio** | 2 | ? |
| **Acid test ratio** | 1 | ? |

**Appendix 3 **

**Three applicants for Marketing Manager for country Z**

|   | Labiba | Shahin | Samihah |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qualifications/Skills | 10 IGCSEs and 3 A levels Speaks 2 languages | 5 IGCSEs and 2 A levels Degree in Business Management | 8 IGCSEs Speaks 6 languages |
| Experience | 5 years working for TT as the Assistant Marketing Manager in country Y | 2 years as the Marketing Manager of a small food company in country Z | 10 years as the Marketing Manager of a large toy company in country Y |

Using the information provided and other relevant factors, consider the **two** strategic options for TechToys Ltd's expansion into Country Z

- Setting up its own factory
- Buying another toy manufacturer

Which option would be the **most profitable**? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2022-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Setting up its own factory has lower initial setup costs of £2.5 million **[Ap]** compared to acquisition costs, allowing TechToys to retain more capital for operations **[An]**. The company can design the facility specifically for multilingual doll production **[Ap]**, ensuring optimal efficiency and quality control from day one **[An]**. TechToys maintains complete control over production processes and company culture **[An]**, which could lead to higher employee satisfaction and productivity. However, the setup will take 18 months **[Ap]**, delaying market entry and potentially losing first-mover advantage to competitors **[An]**. The company lacks local market knowledge and may face regulatory challenges **[An]**.

Buying another manufacturer provides immediate market entry **[Ap]**, allowing TechToys to capture market share quickly and generate revenue sooner **[An]**. The acquired company already has established local supplier relationships and distribution networks **[Ap]**, reducing operational setup time and costs **[An]**. Existing workforce understands local business practices and consumer preferences **[An]**. However, acquisition costs are £4.2 million **[Ap]**, significantly higher than building own factory, reducing available working capital **[An]**. Integration challenges may arise from different company cultures and working practices **[An]**, potentially disrupting production and reducing efficiency **[An]**.

Overall, setting up its own factory is the most profitable option **[E]**. The £1.7 million cost saving compared to acquisition **[Ap]** provides substantial additional working capital for marketing and product development **[E]**. While market entry is delayed, TechToys can use this time to conduct thorough market research and build brand awareness **[Ap]**, ensuring a stronger market position when production begins **[E]**. The custom-built facility will operate at optimal efficiency for multilingual doll production **[E]**, leading to lower long-term operational costs and higher profit margins than adapting an existing manufacturer's processes **[E]**.

> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each option identified in the question:
> - Point: Identify the strategic advantage or disadvantage
> - Evidence (Ap): Apply financial data and case study detail
> - Analysis (An): Explain business impact on profitability
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which option offers better long-term profitability
>   - Justify your choice with financial reasoning
>   - Compare and reject alternatives with clear reasoning
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use financial data and case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly on profitability, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement on most profitable option, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Setting up own factory**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Lower initial investment of £2.5 million **→** more capital available for operations and marketing
>     - Custom design for multilingual doll production **→** optimal efficiency and quality control
>     - Complete control over processes and culture **→** consistent standards and employee motivation
>   - **Drawbacks**
>   
>     - 18-month setup time **→** delayed market entry **→** potential loss of market share to competitors
>     - Lack of local knowledge **→** may face regulatory and cultural challenges
> - **Buying another manufacturer**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Immediate market entry **→** faster revenue generation and market share capture
>     - Established supplier and distribution networks **→** reduced operational setup costs
>     - Existing local workforce **→** understands market preferences and business practices
>   - **Drawbacks**
>   
>     - Higher acquisition cost of £4.2 million **→** less working capital available
>     - Integration challenges **→** potential cultural clashes **→** reduced efficiency
>     - May need to adapt existing processes **→** higher long-term operational costs
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - **Own factory:**
>   
>     - Significant cost savings provide more capital for growth **→** higher long-term profitability
>     - Risk: delayed market entry but allows time for market research and brand building
>   - **Acquisition:**
>   
>     - Faster market entry generates immediate revenue **→** quicker return on investment
>     - Risk: higher costs and integration challenges may reduce overall profitability
>     - TechToys should prioritise long-term profitability over short-term market entry, making own factory the optimal choice for sustainable growth and higher profit margins

parts.problem_md: Do you think making a profit is more important for a business than managing its cash flow? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Making a profit is an important reward for risk-taking and enterprise **[K]**, encouraging owners to invest. Profit can be used as a source of finance for growth and is an important indicator of success. Without profit, businesses may struggle to survive long-term **[An]**

Managing cash flow is vital, because businesses need cash to pay day-to-day costs and ensure liquidity **[K]**. Even if a company is profitable, poor cash flow can lead to problems paying suppliers or employees. This is especially important when sales are made on credit, as money is received later than when costs are incurred **[An]**

Overall, managing cash flow is likely more crucial than making a profit. A company can continue operating in the short term without profit, but without sufficient cash flow, it may be unable to function at all **[E]**. Effective cash flow management ensures the business can keep running and has the opportunity to generate profits in the future **[E]**

>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Profit:
>   
>     - It is a source of finance [k] may increase opportunity for growth [an]
>     - Reward for risk-taking/allows dividend for owners [k] without it, owners will have less incentive to invest [an]
>     - Reward for enterprise [k]
>     - Indicator/measure of success [k]
>     - Important for long-term survival [k]
>   - Cash flow:
>   
>     - Need cash to pay day-to-day costs/ensures liquidity/help avoid cash flow problems/pay debt [k] otherwise might have insufficient funds/working capital to continue production [an]
>     - Sales may be on credit [k] therefore money received later [an]
>     - Reduced need for overdraft [k] which would add to interest costs [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Profit is a reward for risk-taking [k], without it owners will have less incentive to invest [an]. Cash flow is needed to pay day-to-day costs [k] to ensure sufficient inventory to continue production. [an] Managing cash flow is likely to be more important because a business can continue in the short term without making a profit, [eval] but without sufficient cash flow a business may be unable to operate and earn revenue [eval]

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Educational Toys Limited (ETL)**

ETL is a private limited company that manufactures educational toys in Country Y. It has been in business for 15 years and has a reputation for producing high-quality, innovative toys that support children's learning. ETL's main products include interactive science kits, mathematical puzzles, and language learning games for children aged 3-12.

ETL currently sells its products primarily through toy stores and educational supply shops in Country Y. The company has one factory employing 150 workers and uses batch production methods. ETL's sales revenue last year was \$8 million, with a gross profit of \$3.2 million and a net profit of \$800,000.

The CEO of ETL is considering expanding the business by entering the online market and selling directly to consumers through an e-commerce website. This would require an investment of \$500,000 in website development and digital marketing. The finance director has prepared a break-even analysis for this new sales channel, projecting that ETL would need to sell 25,000 units online per year to break even.

ETL is facing increasing competition from imported toys, which are often cheaper but of lower quality. The government of Country Y has recently announced it is considering introducing import tariffs on toys to protect domestic manufacturers.

The company is also aware of growing consumer interest in environmentally friendly and ethically produced toys. ETL's marketing director believes there is an opportunity to rebrand the company as a sustainable toy manufacturer, but this would require changes to production processes and materials.

**Appendix 1: Extract from ETL's income statement for last year (\$000)**

| Sales revenue | 8,000 |
|---|---|
| Cost of sales | 4,800 |
| Gross profit | 3,200 |
| Expenses | 2,400 |
| Profit | 800 |

Consider how each of the following three changes may affect ETL's profit.

- The introduction of import tariffs on toys in Country Y
- An increase in the cost of raw materials
- A decrease in corporate tax rates in Country Y

Which change is likely to have the greatest impact on ETL's profit? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/educational-toys-limited-case-study.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
The introduction of import tariffs on toys in Country Y could be beneficial. As a domestic manufacturer facing increasing competition from imported toys **[Ap]**, ETL would gain a price advantage over imported competitors, potentially allowing them to increase market share and profits **[An]**

An increase in raw material costs would negatively impact ETL's profit. As a toy manufacturer, raw materials are a key cost **[Ap]**. Higher costs would reduce ETL's gross profit margin unless they raise prices, which could hurt sales **[An]**. ETL's gross profit was \$3.2 million last year **[Ap]**, so material cost increases could substantially reduce this

A decrease in corporate tax rates in Country Y would directly increase ETL's net profit. Lower taxes mean ETL keeps more of its pre-tax profit. ETL made \$800,000 net profit last year **[Ap]**, so even a small tax rate reduction could noticeably boost this figure **[An]**

Import tariffs will likely have the greatest positive impact on ETL's profit **[E]**. While lower taxes would help, the tariffs address the key threat of increased overseas competition **[Ap]** and could significantly grow ETL's market share and revenue **[**`equation`**E]**. This has more profit potential than a one-time corporate tax cut **[E]**. The raw material cost increase would hurt profits, making it the least favourable change for ETL, but they may be overcome by making cost reductions elsewhere **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Introduction of import tariffs on toys in Country Y**
> 
>   - Imported competitor toys become more expensive → ETL’s products look cheaper → domestic sales and revenue rise
>   - Tariff protection may allow ETL to raise its own prices slightly → higher gross profit per unit
>   - No direct extra cost for ETL if raw materials are sourced locally
> - **Increase in cost of raw materials**
> 
>   - Raw materials are part of \$4 800 000 cost of sales → any price rise directly cuts gross profit and net profit
>   - Passing costs to customers → risk of lower demand and lost sales
>   - Forces ETL to seek alternative suppliers or negotiate bulk discounts → may strain purchasing function
> - **Decrease in corporate tax rates in Country Y**
> 
>   - Lower tax rate on the \$800 000 profit → net profit after tax increases → more retained earnings for reinvestment
>   - Improves cash flow from tax savings → funds R&D or marketing without borrowing
>   - No effect on gross profit or operational costs
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Increase in raw material costs has the greatest impact on profit because cost of sales is large and any rise sharply reduces both gross and net profit
>   - Import tariffs boost sales and allow price flexibility but depend on competitor responses and do not directly affect costs
>   - Tax rate cuts improve net profit modestly and have the smallest effect on overall profitability

parts.problem_md: Do you think cash or profit is more important for a start-up business? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Cash is vital for start-up businesses. It allows them to pay for essentials like rent, supplies and wages** [K]**. Without enough cash, a start-up might fail, even if it is making a profit on paper, though it may not be enough to encourage an entrepreneur to continue with the risk **[An]**

Profit is also important for start-ups. It shows the business is successful and has potential for growth **[K]**. Profits can be used to expand the business or attract investors. However, profits do not always mean there is cash available immediately **[An]**

For a start-up, cash is more important than profit **[E]**. Cash flow problems can quickly shut down a new business, even if it is profitable. A start-up needs cash to cover daily costs and unexpected expenses. While profit is a good long-term goal, having enough cash is crucial for a start-up to survive and eventually become profitable **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Cash is needed to pay day-to-day expenses [k] → such as rent, supplies, and wages, especially in the early stages of the business [an]
>   - Without enough cash the business may fail [k] → even if it is profitable on paper, the start-up might not survive due to unpaid bills [an]
>   - Profit shows that the business is viable long term [k] → can be used to reinvest, expand, or attract investors to support future growth [an]
>   - Profit does not guarantee available cash [k] → for example, money may be tied up in credit sales or unpaid invoices [an]
> - Evaluation might include:
> 
>   - Cash is more important in the short term [e] → because a lack of liquidity will stop the business operating, whereas profit is more useful once survival is secure [e]
>   - Supported judgement [e]→ cash is more important at the start because survival depends on it, while profit becomes more important as the business grows [e]

parts.problem_md: **Explain four** reasons why profit is important to private sector businesses.
parts.solution_md:
Profit serves as a reward for the risks taken by entrepreneurs and investors **[K]**. Business owners invest time, money, and effort to make their business successful, and profit is their financial compensation **[An]**

Secondly, profit is a useful source of finance **[K] **for businesses. Retained profit can be used to fund the purchase of assets, pay bills, and invest in research and development, helping the business grow **[An]**

Profit is also an indicator of success **[K]**. Increasing profitability suggests that a business is being run effectively and could be an attractive investment opportunity **[An]**

Finally, profit allows businesses to survive and expand in the long term **[K]**. Without profit, a business cannot continue operating or take advantage of growth opportunities **[An]**

>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks

> - Relevant answers might include:
> 
>   - Profit is a reward for risk – entrepreneurs and investors take financial risks when setting up and running a business, and profit is their financial return or incentive for doing so
>   - Profit is a source of finance – retained profit can be reinvested to purchase equipment, fund marketing, support R&D or cover operating expenses
>   - Profit is an indicator of success – a profitable business is likely being run efficiently and may be more attractive to potential investors or lenders
>   - Profit allows for business survival and growth – businesses that generate profit are more likely to stay open, expand, and take advantage of new opportunities
>   - Profit can help to attract investment – investors are more likely to back a business that shows a track record of profitability.
>   - Profit enables dividend payments – in companies with shareholders, profits can be paid out as dividends, helping to retain or attract future investor

Gross profit is the surplus** [K] **of revenue over cost of sales **[K]**
